cases.description: Microsoft's documented example: the largest value in a range where TRUE is counted as 1
cases.expected_note: Excel documents MAXA as evaluating a logical TRUE in a range as 1, so the answer is 1 rather than 0.5; MAX over the same range would return 0.5 because MAX ignores logicals in ranges

cases.description: DIVERGENCE PROBE: all-negative numbers plus a text cell -- Excel counts the text as 0, which becomes the maximum
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's MAXA page carries two remarks that contradict each other for this exact input: 'Arguments that contain text or FALSE evaluate as 0 (zero)' and, one line later, 'Empty cells and text values in the array or reference are ignored'. We assert the text-evaluates-as-0 reading, because AVERAGEA's page carries the identical contradictory pair and settles it with a worked example (28/5 = 5.6) in which range text counts as 0. Under that reading the answer is 0 (0 > -3); under the 'ignored' reading it would be -3. The point of this case is to record which reading each engine actually implements

cases.description: FALSE in a range is evaluated as 0, so it wins over negative numbers
cases.expected_note: Excel documents logical FALSE as 0 for MAXA; 0 > -1 so the maximum is 0

cases.description: A logical typed directly as an argument is also coerced (TRUE -> 1)
cases.expected_note: Excel documents that MAXA evaluates TRUE as 1 whether it comes from a range or is typed as an argument

cases.description: Truly empty cells are ignored (they are not counted as 0)
cases.expected_note: Excel documents empty cells in a reference as ignored by MAXA (this remark is not contradicted elsewhere on the page, unlike the text remark), so the maximum is the largest actual number, -2, and NOT 0

cases.description: A non-numeric string typed directly as an argument is documented as evaluating to 0, which then wins
cases.expected_note: Verbatim from Microsoft's MAXA page: 'Arguments that contain text or FALSE evaluate as 0 (zero)'. Under that rule the literal "abc" becomes 0, which is larger than -5. (MAX's page carries the opposite rule -- text that cannot be translated into numbers causes an error -- so this case checks that an engine applies the A-variant rule and not MAX's)

cases.description: An error value passed as an argument propagates instead of being coerced
cases.expected_note: Error values are not among the things MAXA coerces; NA() produces #N/A and that error is the result of the whole expression
